message.content:
**Yes – you can file a noise complaint with the City of Atlanta.** Atlanta’s local government handles noise violations through its Police Department and the city’s 311 service. Below is a quick guide on how to do it, plus the key contacts and resources you’ll need. --- ## 1. Where to File a Noise Complaint | Service | How to Access | Contact | |---------|---------------|---------| | **Atlanta Police Department – Code Enforcement** | • Call the non‑emergency line
• Use the online 311 portal | Phone: **404‑656‑4000**
Email: **noisecomplaint@atlantaga.gov** | | **City of Atlanta 311 Service** | • Online portal:
• Mobile app “Atlanta 311” (iOS & Android) | Phone: **404‑656‑4000** (same as above) | > **Tip:** If the noise is an emergency (e.g., a fire alarm, ongoing assault, or immediate danger), dial **911**. For non‑emergencies, use the 404‑656‑4000 line or the 311 portal. --- ## 2. How to File a Complaint Online (via 311) 1. **Visit** or open the “Atlanta 311” app. 2. **Select** “Noise Complaint” from the list of services. 3. **Fill out** the form: - **Location** (address or intersection) - **Time** of the disturbance - **Type of noise** (construction, music, barking dogs, etc.) - **Description** (any additional details) 4. **Submit** the form. 5. You’ll receive a confirmation email or text with a reference number. > **Note:** The city may follow up with a police officer or code enforcement officer to investigate. --- ## 3. How to File a Complaint by Phone 1. Call **404‑656‑4000** and say you’d like to file a noise complaint. 2. Provide the same information as above (location, time, type, description). 3. The dispatcher will give you a reference number and tell you what to expect next. --- ## 4. How to File a Complaint by Mail or In Person | Address | Notes | |---------|-------| | **City Hall – Code Enforcement Office**
55 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive
Atlanta, GA 30303 | • Mail: **noisecomplaint@atlantaga.gov**
• In person: Visit the Code Enforcement office during business hours (Mon‑Fri, 8 a.m.‑5 p.m.). | --- ## 5. Key Resources & Ordinances | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | **Atlanta Noise Ordinance (Bylaws)** | | | **City of Atlanta Official Website** | | | **Atlanta 311 Portal** | | | **Police Department Contact Page** | | > The noise ordinance sets limits on decibel levels, defines quiet hours (typically 10 p.m.–7 a.m.), and lists prohibited activities (e.g., loud construction, amplified music). Violations can result in fines or other penalties. --- ## 6. What Happens After You File? 1. **Acknowledgment** – You’ll receive a reference number. 2. **Investigation** – A police officer or code enforcement officer will visit the site. 3. **Resolution** – Depending on the severity, the officer may issue a warning, a citation, or direct the offending party to stop the noise. 4. **Follow‑up** – If the problem persists, you can request a follow‑up inspection or escalation to the city’s Code Enforcement Division. --- ### Quick Checklist - [ ] Identify the exact location and time of the noise. - [ ] Determine if it’s a recurring issue or a one‑time incident. - [ ] Gather any evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings) if possible. - [ ] Choose your preferred filing method (online, phone, mail, in person). - [ ] Keep the reference number for future correspondence. --- **Bottom line:** Yes, you can report a noise complaint to the City of Atlanta. Use the 311 portal or call 404‑656‑4000, provide the necessary details, and the city will take it from there. If you’re dealing with a serious or ongoing issue, consider following up with a police officer or the Code Enforcement office.
